marks.named: a Pong/squash-style paddle game on a grid
deductions: "a single-player Pong/squash-like game" (the fact sheet has an opponent paddle in channel 1)
marks.conclusion: A policy for a paddle game: the paddle sits in column 1 and moves up or down, and the network works out whether the ball is above or below it; outputs 0, 3 and 4 are do-nothing.
marks.judge_notes: Border 1: it reads the untrained border rows and columns as walls whose input never varies. It does not say they are always on or that their rows copy the bias, so this is a generous call. Channel meanings 3: agent (ch0), moving object/ball (ch1) and previous frame (ch4). The ch4 reading is its 'likeliest' and is marked as the least certain part, but it gives a reason (the weights are not an empty-cell pattern), so I credited it. ch2 and ch3 are called untrained and 'constant (e.g. wall) or never occur', which I treated as a hedge worth 0. It does not say ch1 also holds the opponent's paddle. Action meanings 5: up and down are tied to ball-above and ball-below through the A/B pattern, and left/right/no-op are tied to the identical W3 columns plus the paddle being locked to one column. This rests on the standard action order and 'row 1 is the top'; it states both assumptions, and they match the fact sheet. Depth level 3: the A-B axis encodes ball row minus paddle row and drives promote/suppress units on outputs 1 and 2. The fact sheet says the mechanism has not been traced by hand, so I could not check it against the weights, which are not in the folder; I judged it for consistency with the fact sheet's policy and its own cited numbers. Behaviour 4 although it does not mention the reward or the opponent, because it gets what the paddle controls and what it chases, and this matches the fact sheet's 'what a good policy does'. Activation 0: 'ReLU fits but isn't proven' is wrong and not argued from dead units. I did not deduct for it because it is hedged. Training method 1: it leans to a softmax policy trained by REINFORCE/A2C/PPO, with an argument from the absence of a shared state-value component in W3.
